notes: Timing/tokens were not captured: task completion notifications in this environment carried no metrics, so time_seconds/tokens are zeros and deltas are n/a.

Scaffold and audit modes discriminate strongly: eval-0 1.0 vs 0.4 and eval-3 1.0 vs 0.5 (baseline wrote only a README, no doc map, no rule-priority default, no unconfirmed-defaults labeling); eval-1 1.0 vs 0.67.
eval-1 without_skill false positive: it flagged the README<->AGENTS verification/command-table overlap as an SSoT violation - the audience-summary exemption is a real differentiator of the skill.
eval-1 with_skill caught the missing LICENSE gap (composer.json declares MIT); baseline missed it.

eval-2 (STYLE.md review) is a weak discriminator (1.0 vs 0.8): the baseline also caught the AGENTS.md duplications and ESLint-covered rules. The skill's edge here is the 5-point structure coverage and the read-only contract, not finding discovery.
eval-4 (scope override) is non-discriminating (1.0 vs 1.0): a simple fact-fix task both handle correctly. Keep it as a scope-discipline regression canary.

eval-5 (private desktop-app repo full-docs audit, user-requested) ran with_skill only (5/5; 30 findings, 6 corrected files) and is excluded from the benchmark means because it has no baseline counterpart.
All with_skill runs complied with the STYLE.md two-job contract: no authored rules, read-only reviews, empty skeletons.
Single run per configuration - no variance data; rerun flaky-looking evals before trusting deltas.
